text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH

- The far-right National Activism Party (MHP) announces that the son of late chairman Alparslan Turkes will be acting leader until a second congress is held after disputes marred first attempt at the weekend to select a new party chief.
-Turkish Tycoon Asil Nadir arrved in Istanbul on a private flight on Monday night. Nadir is wanted for questioing by the British government in connection with his past business dealings.
MILLIYET
- An Islamist deputy, Mahmut Sonmez resigned from the ruling Islamist Welfare Party. Sonmez said he would join the conservative main opposition party Motherland Party (ANAP).
- Kazakhstan made a suprising statement saying that it would prefer Kazak oil transported to international markets via Turkey.
HURRIYET
- About 500,000 people attended a pro-secularist concert to mark the Youth and Sports holiday.
- Turkish media company Dogan group said they have received just $ 7,500 in state subsidies, denying claims by Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller the figure was many times that.
YENI YUZYIL
- Turkish Armed Forces did not inform the Islamist-led government on its latest cross-border operation into nothern Iraq to combat Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) militants.
- Parliament will consider when to debate a possibe censure motion to topple the Islamist-led government.
RADIKAL

- Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his coalition partner Tansu Ciller were left alone in the standuim where the Youth and Sports Holiday was celebrated on Monday as others in the protocol avoided to salute them.
DUNYA
- Tekel, the state-owned drinks and tobacco producer will be privatised in six months.
- The general manager of Turkish branch of tyre producer Goodyear says Turkish business will grows despite the current political crisis.
ZAMAN
- Dpty PM Ciller says she and Erbakan have agreed she should assume the prime minister's seat now and take the country to fresh elections.
